citations.narrative:
At approximately 6:30am on June 4, 2026, a three-year-old male cynomolgus macaque (ID# CMC050) was injured during
a reconditioning session for pole and collar handling. The technician that performed the session notified the attending
veterinarian, who promptly sedated the animal for examination and determined that the animal sustained a severe break
and significant tissue damage to the left upper arm. The veterinarian elected to perform humane euthanasia at that time
due to the severity of the injury. Necropsy and pathology reports confirmed acute trauma as the cause of the injury. The
facility uses an established Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for performing conditioning sessions; despite
documented training for the technician over this SOP, an IACUC investigation concluded that the technician performed
the session alone, without the assistance of another qualified technician, contrary to instructions within the SOP. The
facility terminated the technician’s employment and performed refresher training for all technicians that handle animals;
the SOP is also in revision to provide further clarity as to procedures and expectations for conditioning activities with non-
human primates.
Failure of the technician to follow procedures resulted in unnecessary pain, suffering and euthanasia for a non-human
primate. The facility must ensure that handling of all animals is done as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a
manner that does not cause trauma, overheating, excessive cooling, behavioral stress, physical harm or unnecessary
discomfort.
CORRECTED BEFORE THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION ON 10/20/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the attending veterinarian and facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
